newsitem.title: GERMANY: Military planners begin Zaire meeting in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Military planners begin Zaire meeting in Germany.

text.p: Military planners began a meeting in Stuttgart on Friday to discuss options for a planned international relief mission to help hundreds of thousands of refugees in Zaire and Rwanda.
Representatives from around 40 countries and non- governmental organisations were expected to attend the conference at Kelly Barracks at the U.S. army base in the southwest German city.
"We're here to discuss the military aspects of the operation," said a spokesman for Canadian forces taking part in the meeting. Canada is coordinating efforts to establish a multinational force.
The spokesman declined to say how long the conference would last. "It will take as long as it takes," he said.
Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy said in Ottawa on Thursday that the meeting would not take any decisions on whether to send a force.
"There will not be a decision in Stuttgart. It is a meeting to look at all the factors and all the options, and after that there will be a context for a decision," Axworthy said.
Several African nations -- including Zimbabwe, Botswana, Cameroon, Senegal and South Africa -- were present at the talks as well as representatives from the major Western powers.
